Independent one-ms class trace and preemptive CPU lock reference
Strict priority can deny all low-class service
L arrives0; high Hk arrives each integerk

Infinite high stream: L never starts

Score = base + floor(age / four ms)
At eight ms: old L ties fresh H8 and wins
Finite H0–H11: L ends9 versus13 ms
High H waits on low L mutex owner
L needs two ms to release; M needs five
Without inheritance: M0–5, L5–7, H7–8

L0–2 at inherited priority; H2–3; M3–8

No extra CPU or GPU interruption implied
Aging delays H8–H11 by one ms in this finite trace; both class schedules drain at thirteen.
Assumptions and actual primitive support bound the claim; safety and final-user proof still apply.
